name: paper_trend_longshort_us_equity_style
hypothesis: Section 'Momentum and Mean Reversion Trading Strategies'. Direction rule, quoted: "Go long when price is above its trend proxy; go short or flat when below, if your venue supports it." Window: 12-month time-series momentum. Hypothesis: the paper's rule - long above the trend proxy, short below - produces a risk-managed, dollar-neutral trend signal that survives stressed costs, and its inverted twin does not.

intake.notes: The paper's long/short rule, tested for the first time. The previously SUPPORTED nasdaq_12m_timeseries_momentum was long_only:true, which CONTRADICTS the paper's own direction rule quoted above. Costs are stressed to 2x the engine default.

signal.params.dead_band.note: 0.0 - no dead band, so the rule is the paper's own: long above the trend proxy, short below. A dead band is an analyst addition and would change the rule being tested.

signal.params.threshold.note: 0.0 - the trend proxy is the sign of the momentum itself, so zero is the paper's rule.

features.momentum.lookback.note: 12-month time-series momentum - the paper names the window: a 12-month time-series momentum for equities and a shorter crypto-adapted window for crypto.

hypothesis.note: Section 'Momentum and Mean Reversion Trading Strategies'. Direction rule, quoted: "Go long when price is above its trend proxy; go short or flat when below, if your venue supports it." Window: 12-mont

universe.preset.note: the US equity style ETFs universe; the papers require the claim to be tested on more than one market because crypto and equities behave differently

portfolio.rebalance.note: monthly. The papers state no cadence; monthly keeps the turnover inside a retail account's cost budget and matches the regime paper's 'swing/daily' horizon.

portfolio.gross_leverage.note: 1.0 - no leverage. The papers do not discuss leverage, so the unlevered result is the one reported.

portfolio.max_position.note: 10% of equity per name. A concentration limit is standard risk management; the papers set no number.

portfolio.vol_target.note: 15% annual volatility target, so the book is sized to a risk level rather than to a dollar amount. The papers set no number.

portfolio.max_names.note: 5 names, so concentration is limited by count as well as by weight.

portfolio.net_target.note: 0.0 - dollar neutral, so a result cannot be a beta bet dressed up as alpha.

portfolio.long_only.note: False - long/short. The regime paper's switching mechanism needs both legs: momentum in trend states and reversal in stress states, and a long-only book cannot express the second. The papers set no direction.

exit.note: The exit is the signal returning to flat. Where the signal has an explicit exit band it is stated in the signal's own params; otherwise the rule is 'the entry condition no longer holds', which is what a regime-conditioned signal means.

signal.params.exit.note: Where the signal carries an exit band it is in its params; otherwise the position closes when the entry condition stops holding. The papers state no exit band for the switching mechanism.

execution.cost_multiplier.note: 2.0 - the STRESSED cost case. A strategy that only survives at typical costs has no edge at retail size; the engine also runs a gross-of-costs stage that separates 'no edge' from 'edge too small to trade'.

period.start.note: 2005-01-01, chosen to cover the 2008 crisis, the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 bear market - the stress regimes the papers say a signal must survive.

name: paper_pairs_meanrev_us_equity_style
hypothesis: Section 'Momentum and Mean Reversion Trading Strategies', subsection on pairs. signal.params.max_pairs.note: 3 pairs. The paper does not say how many; the count is limited so concentration cannot come from one spread.
